t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a flat straight-on UI mockup on deep navy. A centred large light-weight sans headline and a small light subhead in an empty top band. Below, one continuous pale steel-blue double-line pipe snakes across the width over a faint hairline grid, dipping into U-bends that hold text blocks, with P&ID gate valve symbols on the vertical runs. Each block has a mono slash number with hairline rule, an uppercase mono title with status in brackets and a label/value list for <CONTENT>. Flat blueprint line art, no shading, pipe running off the edges.
signature_idea: Open roles sit in the bends of one pipe loop, with a valve between each so open and closed can read as valve state.
strengths: the pipe as connector is an ownable process metaphor for a water company
valve symbols could encode open/closed status meaningfully
navy, steel-blue line art, light headline and mono titles are on-brand
label/value lists keep each role scannable
weaknesses: valves are decorative; they do not reflect each role's status
invented pay figures, locations and reference codes
body text is small and dense inside the bends
rounded pipe bends and background grid add noise
brand_fit_why: Navy blueprint with one steel-blue pipe, light headline and mono labels fits the brand, but duplicated content and meaningless valves reduce precision.
